# iofs

```go
import "github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/iofs"
```

Package iofs presents a [github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7.Location](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/#Location>) as a read\-only [io/fs.FS](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#FS>).

It lets any VFS backend be used wherever the standard library accepts a filesystem, such as [net/http.FileServerFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/#FileServerFS>), [html/template.ParseFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/html/template/#ParseFS>), [io/fs.WalkDir](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#WalkDir>) and [io/fs.Glob](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#Glob>):

```
loc, _ := vfssimple.NewLocation("s3://bucket/assets/")
fsys := iofs.New(loc)

http.Handle("/", http.FileServerFS(fsys))
data, err := fs.ReadFile(fsys, "config/app.json")
```

The returned filesystem also implements [io/fs.StatFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#StatFS>), [io/fs.ReadDirFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#ReadDirFS>), [io/fs.ReadFileFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#ReadFileFS>) and [io/fs.SubFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#SubFS>). It needs no change to any backend, and it never writes.

### Names

Names follow [io/fs.ValidPath](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#ValidPath>): unrooted, slash\-separated, without "." or ".." elements, with "." naming the location the filesystem was built on. On Windows a name containing a backslash is also invalid, as with [os.DirFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/os/#DirFS>), because the os backend treats it as a separator, and a listed name containing one is omitted from ReadDir. Invalid names fail with an error matching [io/fs.ErrInvalid](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#ErrInvalid>) before any request is made.

### Files and directories

A name is resolved by listing its parent directory with [github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list.Entries](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list/#Entries>), so the same rules hold on every backend, including those with no real directories. When a name matches both a file and a directory, which object stores allow, the file wins \(except for Sub, which makes no request and so cannot tell\). A listed name that is not an [io/fs.ValidPath](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#ValidPath>) element, such as an object key "a//b", cannot be represented and is silently omitted from ReadDir and [io/fs.WalkDir](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#WalkDir>). Object stores cannot represent an empty directory: a directory exists only while something is stored beneath it.

A symbolic link is reported as the listing reports it: with [io/fs.ModeSymlink](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#ModeSymlink>) and without being followed, so a link to a directory is not a directory here, unlike with [os.DirFS](<https://pkg.go.dev/os/#DirFS>), and opening a link fails with [io/fs.ErrInvalid](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#ErrInvalid>). Links in the intermediate components of a name are resolved by the backend, so on the os backend a link inside the root can lead outside it; do not serve an untrusted tree that may contain such links. The same holds for Sub.

[io/fs.FileInfo.Sys](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#FileInfo.Sys>) always returns nil, so the writable [github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7.File](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/#File>) behind an entry is never reachable.

A location that does not exist cannot be told apart from an empty one when it is opened as ".", so ReadDir on it returns no entries and no error; names beneath it do not exist.

### Cost

Opening or statting a name costs one listing request. Entries returned by ReadDir carry the size and modification time the backend listed, so walking a tree and reading entry metadata needs no per\-file request on backends that list natively. On a backend that does not, the first Info call for each entry costs the requests Size and LastModified make. Prefer ReadDir over many Stat calls when metadata for a whole directory is needed.

### Context

[io/fs.FS](<https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs/#FS>) methods take no context. Use [WithContext](<#WithContext>) to supply the one used for listing; it defaults to [context.Background](<https://pkg.go.dev/context/#Background>). Retries are left to each backend.

<a name="New"></a>
## func New

```go
func New(loc vfs.Location, opts ...Option) fs.FS
```

New returns a read\-only fs.FS rooted at loc. The name "." refers to loc itself.

The result also implements fs.StatFS, fs.ReadDirFS, fs.ReadFileFS and fs.SubFS.

<a name="Option"></a>
## type Option

Option configures the filesystem returned by New.

```go
type Option func(*fsys)
```

<a name="WithContext"></a>
### func WithContext

```go
func WithContext(ctx context.Context) Option
```

WithContext sets the context used for the listing requests behind Open, Stat and ReadDir. The default is context.Background\(\).
